# C2 validation capture provenance

The ordered loop uses source HEAD 4b13b64a0f4556470cbf6b7a5e1c7f1b000d0f50,
staged source tree 1e76097a22d620a9f3839ff0c0d49f1f3d636d68, exec session95914,
and the preserved validate-1e76097a.ps1 command script. It is ordinary leased
validation, not a benchmark. The original Start-Transcript file
full-loop-1e76097a.log is PRIVATE AND UNSAFE FOR PUBLICATION: Windows captured
ambient concurrent console/TUI text. It must not be copied, quoted, included
in a manifest for publication or used as scoped verification evidence. Root
confirmed this exclusion and continuation of the same running loop.

Scoped evidence instead consists of the actual exec/write_stdin result
chunks saved separately as full-loop-1e76097a-scoped-*.log. Each identifies
session/chunk/status and original token count. CRLF is normalized to LF for
repository hygiene; no substantive output is removed. Empty polls have no
output to archive. The initial scoped chunk140e9b was mechanically recovered
and compared to response record4160 in the author's original Codex session:
rollout-2026-09-14T15-19-02-01a0a124-dae5-7af0-a042-27ecb5260222.jsonl.
It was not copied from the unsafe transcript. No new execution is implied by
recovering a receipt.

An initial manual copy introduced a typo in one duplicated HEAD line. A
patch with incorrect expected text failed verification, then the correction
matched. A subsequent attempt to delete/add that same path in one patch was
rejected by apply_patch. The final file's complete output body was then
mechanically compared to the actual original response and matched. These
are private evidence-authoring diagnostics, not Cargo failures; the original
session receipt remains authoritative. No commit/publication contained the
incorrect copy and no runtime input changed.

The six original development command/result receipts are recovered separately
in development-original-receipts.jsonl, with source line/hash, exact command,
execution status and actual output. They cover initial missing-module TDD,
fixture Git/source-byte mismatch, unsupported Windows timestamp operation,
the fixture PATH error, unused import, and whitespace diagnostic. The last
wrapper exited0 despite the inner diff diagnostic; its status is not silently
changed to nonzero. Historical failure logs and summaries remain preserved.
This targeted recovery does not claim an audit of the entire author session.
